findings.summary: The test's copy of the secret patterns leaves out two of the kit scanner's patterns, so a template containing either still passes terraform test, although the real scan catches them.
No test checks that the Elastic IP association resource exists; removing it leaves terraform test passing.
No test can guard against an output that exposes the user data or another secret-bearing value; review is the only check.
Because the data mount is nofail, Docker can start containers on reboot before the data volume is mounted; an ordering drop-in on the Docker service would remove the race.
Caddy's TLS and ACME account keys sit inside the directory that is bind-mounted into the Postgres container, whose entrypoint runs as root.
The Caddy repository key check reads only the first fingerprint, while apt then trusts every key in the downloaded keyring.
Two install steps in the bootstrap end with a guard that also hides a failure to install the apt source or the cron file.
The README paragraph on replacement states an AWS behaviour of the volume attachment without the inline VERIFY marker that main.tf carries.
The verify gate's weakened-test check does not look at Terraform test files, so a removed assertion in a .tftest.hcl file would not be flagged.
The Engineer applied some main.tf edits with a one-off script instead of the edit tool, against the command-shape rule; the result was reviewed and is the same.
